setup.Tool / version: Verified with OpenROAD from the OpenROAD-flow-scripts Docker image openroad/orfs:v3.0-941-g3395328e (sha256:59c7d95ded17bf86a8882460eebc1e4a1e15e6b5ae763a362a7e2cafce209fe1; the binary reports 'HEAD-HASH-NOTFOUND' as its version). Only OpenROAD/OpenSTA commands are used; no yosys.
setup.Files:
netlists/<case>.v : the contest netlists rewritten 1:1 onto unit_delay.lib cells (same instance names, net names and ports; and/or/nand/nor/xor/xnor/not/buf -> AND2/OR2/NAND2/NOR2/XOR2/XNOR2/INV/BUF with pins Y,A,B; dff -> DFF with CLK,RN,SN,D,Q).
unit_delay.lib : every gate has delay exactly 1, so a path's arrival time = number of gates on it (DFF CLK->Q also = 1).
unit_delay.lef : dummy abstracts; OpenROAD refuses to link without a LEF ('no technology has been read').
orhelp.tcl : small helper procs used below (putl prints one item per line: long single-line output can come out garbled in OpenROAD) (full text at the bottom of this sheet).
setup.[LOAD] (start of every test):
read_lef unit_delay.lef
read_liberty unit_delay.lib
read_verilog netlists/<case>.v
link_design top
source orhelp.tcl
setup.Conventions:
Put net/port names in braces so Tcl doesn't treat [ ] as commands: {n42[0]}.
node <name> = the port if <name> is a primary I/O, else the pin driving that net.
get_fanin / get_fanout stop at flip-flops and INCLUDE the boundary DFF; `inst_names ... comb` drops DFFs (combinational cone, DFF Q = primary input).
report_checks -unconstrained: 'Actual Delay' / 'data arrival time' = gate depth. 'No paths found.' = no path. Paths starting at a DFF include its CLK->Q stage: subtract 1 (gdepth does this automatically).
Constants: OpenROAD turns 1'b1 / 1'b0 into nets named one_ / zero_.

summary.commands:
[LOAD]
putl [const_loads 1 NAND2]                            ;# cells of a type with an input tied to 1'b1
putl [const_loads 0 AND2]                             ;# ... tied to 1'b0
putl [lsort -unique [concat [const_loads 1 NOR2] [const_loads 0 NOR2]]]   ;# any constant
putl [const_loads 1]                                  ;# every cell (incl. DFF SN pins) tied to 1
summary.verified: Prompts test32/36/37/39 (real designs: constants only on DFF pins; test37 = 2,324 DFFs) and 25 synthetic cases with gates tied to constants: exact.
summary.notes: Relies on OpenROAD naming the constant nets one_ / zero_.

summary.commands:
[LOAD]

summary.commands:
[LOAD]
# gates driven by a gate (use /Q for a DFF):
putl [inst_names [get_cells -of_objects [get_pins -of_objects [get_nets -of_objects [get_pins <GATE>/Y]] -filter "direction==input"]]]
# gates driven directly by a net or primary input:
putl [inst_names [get_cells -of_objects [get_pins -of_objects [get_nets {<NET>}] -filter "direction==input"]]]
# highest-fanout nets (load pins), constants excluded; add  && [llength [get_ports -quiet [get_full_name $n]]]  to rank inputs only
set rows {}
foreach n [get_nets *] { if {[get_full_name $n] in {one_ zero_}} continue
  lappend rows [list [get_full_name $n] [llength [get_pins -quiet -of_objects $n -filter "direction==input"]]] }
putl [lrange [lsort -integer -decreasing -index 1 $rows] 0 4]

summary.notes: get_nets -of_objects does not accept ports; use the net name, which equals the port name. Report ties.
